title: Last weekend
subtitle: How was your weekend? — the past simple with -ed
canDo: I can talk about my weekend with -ed verbs.
I can spell past verbs: worked, lived, studied, stopped.
I can hear and say -ed in three ways.
teacherNotes: Düzenli fiillerle past simple. -ed'in üç okunuşuna (/t/, /d/, /ɪd/) özellikle zaman ayırın: Türk ve Arap öğrenciler çoğu zaman her fiilde /ɪd/ der (walk-id, play-id).
Kural: /ɪd/ sadece t veya d ile biten fiillerde (visited, wanted, started). Diğerlerinde tek hece: walked = "wokt".
Ürdün'de hafta sonu Cuma ve Cumartesi; Lina'nın mesajı bu kültürel farkı konuşmak için iyi bir fırsat. Türkiye'de ve ABD'de Cumartesi–Pazar.
Did'li soru ve olumsuzlar 8.3 ve 8.4'te geliyor; bu derste sadece olumlu cümle ve How was …? kullanın.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: My weekend in Amman
sections.intro: A message from Lina to her brother, Omar.
paragraphs: Hi Omar! In Jordan, the weekend is Friday and Saturday, remember? So here's my weekend news.
On Friday, we visited Grandma Fatima. She cooked maqluba for twelve people!
I helped in the kitchen, and after lunch, we talked for hours.
In the evening, Mom and I walked in the city center together.
On Saturday, I studied all day. I have an exam on Sunday!
Then I called Kareem and played with little Adam on video. He's so loud!
What about your weekend? Call me!

sections.title: Lina's weekend
sections.instructions: Read again. Match the two parts.

sections.title: Grammar: the past simple with -ed
look: On Saturday, I **cooked** for my neighbors.
I **called** my family and **talked** to my grandmother.
rules: Past simple: finished actions in the past (**yesterday**, **last week**, **on Saturday**).
The same form for all people: I / you / he / she / we / they work**ed**.
Say -ed three ways: /t/ walk**ed**, cook**ed** · /d/ play**ed**, call**ed** · /ɪd/ visit**ed**, want**ed** (after t and d).

support.tr: Past simple geçmişte bitmiş işler içindir (-di'li geçmiş): I worked = Çalıştım. Düzenli fiillere -ed eklenir ve her kişide aynıdır: I / she / they worked. Türkçede kişi eki değişir (çalıştım, çalıştı, çalıştılar), İngilizcede değişmez. -ed çoğu zaman ayrı bir hece değildir: walked "vokt" gibi okunur. Sadece t ve d ile biten fiillerde /id/ olur: visited.
support.ar: نستخدم past simple للأفعال التي انتهت في الماضي: I worked = عملتُ. نضيف ed إلى الفعل المنتظم، وهو نفسه مع كلّ الضمائر: I / she / they worked. في العربية يتغيّر الفعل (عملتُ، عملتْ، عملوا)، أمّا في الإنجليزية فلا يتغيّر. وغالبًا لا تكون ed مقطعًا جديدًا: walked تُنطق /wɔːkt/. نقول /id/ فقط بعد t و d مثل visited.

tr.note: yesterday, last week, on Saturday gibi kelimeler varsa fiil geçmiş olmalı. was ile -ed'i birlikte kullanma.
wrong: Yesterday I work at the café.
right: Yesterday I worked at the café.

ar.note: لا تنطق ed دائمًا /id/، ولا تنسَ كتابة ed.
wrong: Last week she visit her aunt.
right: Last week she visited her aunt.
